If you are an experienced candidate you should be knowing about this already. Keeping my Judgement aside, every salaried person must know how to read their payslip to keep a track of where their money is going. Even though MNC like Infosys will barely make mistakes in their payslip, but still it is a useful skill to have. Going through your salary slip: This is your Monthly Earnings, and as you predicted it is around 95k per month. But you should remember this Monthly earning ≠ In hand salary. In hand salary = monthly earning - monthly deductions(including taxes) 74,545 = 95172 - 20627 Here is the section showing your monthly deductions: All these are included in your CTC. Now you might be wondering, why are they deducting PF from our earnings since it is a separate component in your CTC. It is just part of your contribution to PF. The Employee contribution of 12% is cut from your monthly earnings whereas another 12% is paid by your employer which is the component highlighted separately in your CTC. Now comes the elephant in the room, TAXES. You are paying 10,188 per month as taxes. The calculation of your taxes is mentioned in this portion of your payslip: This looks a bit alarming to me since you are paying more tax than you should because of a lack of proper taxation knowledge. Let me help you with that too. You can calculate your tax by going to this gov website: The first thing you should remember is there are 2 tax regimes available, one is old regime and the other is new regime. This is pointed out by this entry in the calculator: If you are choosing no, that means you are opting for old regime. If yes, new regime. The main difference in short: Old regime: More deductions allowed, more tax to be paid on net income New regime: Fewer deductions allowed, less tax to be paid on net income These schemes can be chosen at the start of the year in your company portal or next year at the time of IT filing(In that case, if you had paid more taxes you will get a return). Looking at your payslip, you have chosen the old scheme and paid a total tax of 1,22,254 and 10188 monthly. But if you change your tax structure to new regime: You will be paying 1,07,550 as total tax and thus a reduction of almost 15k. Notice I have put more in net taxable income as there are no deductions allowed. Or If you want to continue with old tax regime, please proceed to make more contributions under certain sections as per the IT act and you can bring down your net taxable income and thus your tax. These are mentioned here, and as you can see, you do not seem to utilize the benefits. Thus I think new regime would be more beneficial to you if you don't want to keep the headache of systematic investing(But I think every person should do). Taxation is a very vast topic in itself and is a whole other conversation. Question: What are working hours in the Indian IT industry?
Answer: Short Answer: Somewhere between 9AM and 10 PM Long answer: There is no fixed working hour in Indian IT industry. Though some company mandates a minimum 9–10 hours in office, it totally depends on many factors like the company, the project you are working on, the client location, location of other team members, your manager, your seniority, any shift you are working on. I will tell you my story. When I was a fresher, I used to work from 10–6. I used to get annoyed when my lead/manager made me stay beyond 6. After 3 years, I used to work for a client who was in Japan and the project team was in Canada. So I had to wake up early to have meetings with client, do my own work in Indian day time. Attend a meeting at 7 with my project team in Canada log out by 8. Fast forward 3 years more, I am working for a UK client, so my official timing is 12–9:30. But most days I login by 10 and stay till 10 because of work pressure and not because anyone asked me to do it. The only thing good about the industry is you don't need to stay glued to your screen for the entire 10–12 hours. As long as you complete your work no one really cares if you take a break of 2/3 hours in between or go for a stretch or walk. All you need to do is to attend meetings and complete your work on time(though there are some exceptions where manager and companies treat employees like students in school, but those are rare). Hope I could resolve your query.
